source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Login to WebUI and go to KVM page.
2. Try to using keyboard and mouse to control system for a long time.
EX: User can use KVM for one week to check the stablility.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor Reading & Threshold is human reable and match with spec.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO correctly recognizes the interactive GUI and human visual-feedback boundary, but it does not expose that the Sensor Reading/Threshold Criteria cannot judge KVM input, that `long time` and the one-week example are unbounded, or that safe target/input and session-stability evidence are undefined.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY / IMPROVED correctly retains a human interactive core and proposes safe marker, focus, pointer, latency and soak evidence. V3.1 additionally records a source conflict, refuses to convert an example one-week soak into a fixed requirement, distinguishes input-function coverage from endurance coverage, and requires an engineer-approved acceptance matrix before formal execution.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 906/2291 preserves NO/manual status but repeats the unrelated Sensor Reading Criteria and offers only post-test photos, with no duration, input matrix, SUT identity, latency, disconnect or recovery contract.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: The next multi-user KVM case covers concurrent-session capacity, not keyboard/mouse fidelity. Other KVM/video/virtual-media cases cannot substitute input event delivery or long-duration stability.

historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the contradictory Master Criteria; ED-34 makes duration, client/platform matrix and expected behavior Project inputs; ED-35 prevents unsafe/destructive input or false coverage from a short read-only check; ED-38 requires evidence preservation, no retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Interactively verify the BMC remote KVM forwards representative keyboard and mouse input to the intended SUT reliably, including focus and pointer behavior and an engineer-defined stability interval, while preserving the distinction between a functional input check and any separately approved long-duration soak.
original_method: A human operator logs into the correct BMC WebUI KVM, verifies target identity, sends an approved non-destructive keyboard/mouse action matrix and visually confirms the exact SUT response. If endurance coverage is required, the operator follows an approved observation/idle/reconnect schedule for a defined duration rather than assuming the source's one-week example is mandatory.
manual_activity: A human must control the actual remote KVM client and visually verify keyboard/mouse responses, focus and pointer alignment on the intended SUT. The agent may prepare the checklist and collect available logs, but cannot replace end-to-end interactive perception. Engineering must define valid KVM criteria and whether a functional check, soak, or both are required.
required_inputs: Engineer-approved KVM-specific Criteria and explicit treatment of the unrelated Master Sensor Reading text
Scope decision for short functional input coverage versus long-duration stability coverage
Exact duration, observation cadence, active/idle periods, reconnect schedule, interruption/latency limits and failure-stop rule
BMC/SUT asset identity, KVM implementation and versions, client endpoint/browser/plugin, host OS/display and network path
Safe test application/marker plus keyboard layout, key/modifier/function/repeat and mouse click/drag/wheel/pointer matrix
Expected visible results, prohibited power/reset/security/destructive sequences, session cleanup and recovery
Screenshot/video, timestamp, client/browser console, BMC audit, host input/application and operator observation evidence plan
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC, KVM, browser, host or audit logs; prior disconnects and input faults are relevant.
Confirm the BMC and visible SUT identity before sending any key or pointer action; never rely on window title alone.

Use a dedicated safe application or test marker. Prohibit power/reset shortcuts, firmware/BIOS navigation, destructive shell commands, credential entry, security changes and uncontrolled click/drag targets.
Do not claim a short input demonstration proves the source's long-time or one-week stability example; report the exact observed duration and coverage difference.
Do not leave keys/buttons logically pressed, a privileged session unlocked or the KVM open after operator handoff. Define session timeout/reconnect and stuck-input recovery.
Stop and preserve first-failure evidence on lost/duplicated/stuck events, wrong target, severe latency, frozen video, disconnect or unexpected SUT action; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare the approved asset/client/version inventory, safe input checklist, prohibited-action list, evidence timestamps and failure/recovery rules; do not drive the interactive KVM core.
Collect available BMC audit/session metadata, browser console/network data and host-side application/input logs while the operator performs each approved key and mouse action.
Correlate operator-recorded visible responses, focus/pointer state, latency, lost/duplicate/stuck events and reconnect behavior with timestamps; distinguish short functional and soak evidence.
Archive redacted evidence and verify session closure and unchanged system state; do not execute KVM input, clear logs, power/reset the DUT, retry automatically or assign a verdict.
engineer_actions: Replace the unrelated Sensor Reading/Threshold Criteria in the Review layer with KVM input-function and stability acceptance while preserving Master source, and decide the functional-versus-soak scope.
Approve duration/cadence/client/input/latency/disconnect/recovery matrix and safe marker/prohibited actions.
Perform or supervise the manual GUI interactions, confirm visible SUT responses and issue the formal verdict with exact achieved duration and uncovered coverage.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The NO/manual conclusion is appropriate for the available non-GUI agent path, but its note is incomplete because it does not resolve the invalid Criteria, ambiguous duration, safe action set, target identity, evidence or recovery.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No CLI substitute. Use a human-operated, version-recorded KVM session on a verified SUT with an approved non-destructive input matrix and, if required, a separately scheduled stability soak with explicit observations and reconnect checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The KVM mouse/keyboard purpose, WebUI path, `long time` wording, one-week example, unrelated Criteria, no Script, DeepSeek NO and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not reinterpret the example as an automatic fixed duration or overwrite Master.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Define two checkpoints if both are required: a bounded functional matrix for event fidelity/focus/pointer behavior and a separately scheduled soak with periodic active probes, idle/session-timeout and reconnect observations.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC remote-KVM implementation, client/browser/plugin and target SUT/OS/display combination approved by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/KVM firmware, browser/client/plugin, client OS/input devices, SUT BIOS/OS/display and network-path versions/settings.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project remote-KVM requirements, BMC vendor KVM manual/compatibility matrix, security/session policy and approved endurance test plan.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Converts vague repeated use into a measurable input matrix and optional evidence-backed soak while preserving human end-to-end interaction.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A short matrix does not prove one-week stability; a passive open session does not prove continuous input fidelity; one browser/layout does not cover all supported clients.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Corrected criteria, scope/duration decision, client/input matrix, measurable limits, evidence cadence and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong-window input can affect the DUT, long sessions may expire or monopolize KVM capacity, and client/browser automation cannot replace human visual confirmation unless separately qualified.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use an approved GUI-automation or KVM test harness for repeatable input injection and telemetry, but it must retain the original human end-to-end method, document client/target/version and engineer approval, prove equivalent key/mouse/visual feedback and session-duration coverage, and preserve a manual boundary for perceptual pointer/focus anomalies. A short automated probe is only partial evidence for a long soak.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT/client asset and version identities, approved KVM-specific Criteria, scope/duration/cadence and safe input matrix
Redacted screenshots or recording showing correct target and each representative key/mouse action with expected versus visible response, focus and pointer alignment
Timestamped latency, lost/duplicated/stuck event, video/focus/pointer, idle/session-timeout, disconnect/reconnect and recovery observations for the exact achieved duration
Browser/client console/network, BMC audit/session and host application/input logs with preservation hashes and no-clear proof
Explicit functional-versus-soak and client-matrix coverage statement, safe session cleanup/unchanged DUT state and engineer-owned PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title and Procedure test interactive KVM keyboard/mouse stability, but the Criteria judges sensor readings and thresholds, which cannot accept or reject any KVM input behavior. The duration is also ambiguous because `long time` is undefined and one week is presented only as an example.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Formal execution readiness is pending an engineer-approved KVM Criteria and scope, but the intended interactive operation and safe manual boundary are identifiable. The conflict can be resolved in the Review/Project Test Plan without altering Master, so it is not treated as an irreducible permanent BLOCKED case.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains NO/manual core but adds the missing source conflict, scope/duration decision, safe action set and evidence/recovery contract.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on MANUAL ONLY and strengthens it by making Criteria correction engineer-owned and by separating functional and endurance acceptance rather than treating the one-week example casually.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic photos with target-bound input, latency, session and duration evidence and rejects the unrelated Criteria.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps multi-user capacity, video and virtual-media coverage separate from keyboard/mouse event fidelity.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact case.

review_improvement: Prevents sensor-threshold wording or a brief successful click from being presented as KVM keyboard/mouse stability, and prevents vague one-week use from becoming an unowned, unsafe or unauditable requirement.
independent_technical_reasoning: End-to-end KVM input requires a real client, video feedback, focus and pointer perception and a safe target application; SSH cannot demonstrate that path. Stability is a time-based claim requiring defined probes and failure limits. Because the supplied Criteria measures an unrelated sensor domain, the Master must be preserved while engineering supplies a KVM-specific acceptance contract before execution can receive a verdict.
